John the Baptist was born with a great destiny. John was supposed to prepare the way for the Messiah and make his path easy. (Matthew 3:3) But, though John preached and baptized in the wilderness in preparation for the Messiah (in fulfillment of Isaiah 40:3), when it came time for John to become Jesus' first disciple after having received the revelation that Jesus is the Messiah (John 1:33-34), John flakes out and doesn't follow Jesus. Later, when the Jewish leaders ask John if he is Elijah, he doesn't take the opportunity to say he is and then testify about Jesus being the Messiah. Instead, he rambles on about being a “voice in the wilderness calling to make straight the way for the Lord.” (John 1:19-23) Even more pathetic, we later find John in prison wondering if Jesus is “the one or should we look elsewhere?” ( Matthew 11:2-3)

“For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John. And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come. Whoever has ears, let them hear.” Matthew 11:13-15

Here was the most important prophet of God's dispensation and he blew it. What went wrong? Why couldn't John get his facts straight? Why couldn't he give up his “career” and follow Jesus? To answer these questions, we need to understand who John's parents were and what relationship they had to Jesus.

John's father was Zechariah, the High Priest of Jerusalem. His mother, Elizabeth, was the cousin of Jesus' mother Mary. As the following passage shows, Elizabeth knew who Jesus was:

“At that time Mary got ready and hurried to a town in the hill country of Judea, where she entered Zechariah’s home and greeted Elizabeth. When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. In a loud voice she exclaimed: 'Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the child you will bear! But why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? As soon as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy. Blessed is she who has believed that the Lord would fulfill his promises to her!'” Luke 1:39-45

Considering the importance of this Holy Spirit revelation, wouldn't Elizabeth have shared her good news with John as he grew up? If she had, wouldn't John have grown up knowing that Jesus was to be the Messiah. But as John 1:31 shows, John didn't know Jesus was the Messiah until the “Spirit descended from heaven like a dove.” What's more, considering Zechariah was the High Priest of Jerusalem, wouldn't Elizabeth had made sure that her husband knew about her revelation? And, then, wouldn't Zechariah have made sure to announce the revelation to all of Israel? If he had, wouldn't Jesus have been treated like the king that he was to become?

“For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” Isaiah 9:6

Furthermore, when the Magi had arrived with gifts, wouldn't they have found Jesus being pampered with all that Israel had to offer a king of kings?

“After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem and asked, 'Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.'” Matthew 2:1-2

“On coming to the house, they saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh.” Matthew 2:11
